subject: Algorithm32 Paper J4 experimental Lebedev-38 incoming-quadrature candidate
profileSelection: The candidate changes only the incident angular quadrature from pinned equal-weight Fibonacci-34 to the antipodally closed ninth-degree Lebedev-38 rule. The paper physical profile, W27 outgoing domain, 48 physical altitude nodes, Jthrough4 recurrence, numerical controls, measurements, and score thresholds remain unchanged. These rules are fixed before candidate output is generated.

spectralBoundary.nativeRepresentation: 40 point-sampled spectral-radiance-density channels at the paper coordinates lambda_i = 360 + 11.75*i nanometers for i=0..39
spectralBoundary.benchmarkProjection: Identity; no spectral fit, scale, RGB conversion, or 15-to-40 projection is applied.

rules: Output validity requires all 17 by 81 directional spectra and derived irradiances to be finite and nonnegative.
B1 is favorable at or below the published-model medians, limited at or below the upper quartiles, and adverse otherwise.
B2 is favorable only when RMSE, absolute bias, and worst absolute residual are all at or below their medians; limited only when all are at or below their upper quartiles; and adverse otherwise.
B3 must reproduce B1 aggregate RMSE within 0.000001 mW m^-2 sr^-1 nm^-1 and retain exactly the four declared mismatch fields.
The whole-algorithm classification uses the same favorable, limited, and adverse aggregation rule as the frozen Paper J4 baseline.

The candidate may not be preferred merely because its Flat180 render is more symmetric. It must be rescored against the comparison-paper measurements, and its scores must be reported beside the unchanged Paper J4 Fibonacci-34 baseline.
